findings.explanation: ServiceNow's Major Incident Management plugin (com.snc.incident.mim) marks major incidents with `major_incident_state` (Proposed, Accepted, Rejected, Canceled) and adds a Post Incident Report tab. There is no out-of-the-box `major_incident` field, and `u_major_incident` exists only as a site customisation. The text also never names the post-mortem fields or the sourcetype.
findings.suggested_fix: Say: `index=itsm sourcetype=snow:incident` from Splunk_TA_snow, with major incidents identified by `major_incident_state="accepted"` when MIM is active (or a site-specific `u_` flag otherwise). Name the post-incident-review completion field or the related task table used to track the review.

findings.explanation: The post-mortem completion field has three different names. The implementation uses `u_post_mortem_complete`, while the SPL uses `post_mortem_completed` and `u_post_mortem_date`. The data sources also offer `major_incident`, which the SPL never uses (it filters on `u_major_incident`).
findings.quote: Align field names with your form (`u_post_mortem_complete`, tasks, etc.).
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one documented field set (for example the MIM `major_incident_state` plus one post-mortem completion field) and use the same names in implementation, data sources and detailed implementation. Flag the SPL so it matches as well.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified, but every compliance `evidenceArtifact` says "Auto-drafted — SME review required", most prose fields are template text, and the field names disagree across fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the status to draft or unverified until an SME confirms the field mapping and the compliance claims.

findings.explanation: The text contains two concatenated copies of Steps 1 to 4, and the second is generic boilerplate. It contradicts the UC: the SPL uses `earliest=-90d` and the implementation asks for a weekly report, not paging. It also suggests a spot-check of `compliant`, a field the SPL computes and then never uses. Nothing explains how to join a post-mortem child task when the review is tracked as a separate record.
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one set of steps: ingest `incident` (and the post-mortem task table if one is used) with Splunk_TA_snow, take the latest event per `number`, run weekly over 90 days, and report the compliance percentage and overdue major incidents per assignment group.

findings.explanation: The false positives (maintenance windows, synthetic probes, `host`) have nothing to do with post-mortem tracking.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `itsm` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: post-mortems recorded in a problem record, child task or external document rather than on the incident form; incidents demoted from major (`major_incident_state=canceled`) after closure; older snapshot events from before the post-mortem flag was set (Splunk_TA_snow indexes every update); policy waivers for duplicate or child major incidents; and reopened incidents whose `resolved_at` moved.

findings.explanation: ServiceNow incident data is collected by Splunk_TA_snow (Splunkbase 1928) REST inputs on a heavy forwarder or search head, not by a Universal Forwarder modular input or scripted poll.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Say the data is collected by the Splunk_TA_snow `incident` table input (Splunkbase 1928) into `index=itsm`.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `state="closed"` probably never matches. ServiceNow incident `state` is an integer choice (6 = Resolved, 7 = Closed), and the subcategory guide's own SPL filters on `state=6`. Resolved-but-not-yet-closed major incidents are also excluded. `resolved_at + 7*86400` assumes epoch seconds, but ServiceNow date-times usually arrive as strings and need `strptime`.

The `compliant` eval is computed but never used, and its OR with `isnotnull(u_post_mortem_date)` conflicts with the final `where post_mortem_completed=false`. There is no per-`number` latest reduction, so a stale pre-completion snapshot keeps flagging an incident that has since completed its post-mortem. Major incidents are identified by `u_major_incident` rather than the out-of-the-box `major_incident_state`.

The entries are duplicated: APRA CPS 234 §23 and §36, MAS TRM §8.1.1 and UK NIS Reg.11 each appear twice, once under a slug regulation id and once under a display name. CPS 234 §36 and UK NIS Reg.11 are regulator-notification obligations, so post-mortem completion does not evidence timely notification; `mode: satisfies` overclaims for those clauses.

summary: The goal (closed major incidents with no post-mortem 7 days after resolution) is clear, but the major-incident and post-mortem fields are named differently in every field and do not match ServiceNow's out-of-the-box Major Incident Management fields. The detailed implementation and false positives are generic template text, and the UC is marked `verified` while its own compliance artefacts say "SME review required".
